# windows_firewall_profile (Resource)

Manages a Windows Defender Firewall profile (`Domain`, `Private` or `Public`) on a remote Windows host via SSH and PowerShell (`NetSecurity` module). A profile always exists — Windows creates it with the OS — so creating this resource never provisions anything new: it only tunes the profile's settings in place, and deleting it makes no remote change unless `restore_on_destroy` is set.

Only the attributes configured in Terraform are written (`Set-NetFirewallProfile -PolicyStore PersistentStore`); every other setting on the host is left untouched and undiffed. Group Policy owns the `ActiveStore` view: when a GPO manages a profile, what `Get-NetFirewallProfile` reports (ActiveStore) can diverge from what Terraform writes (PersistentStore), and GPO-managed `NotConfigured` tri-states are observed as unset rather than exposed as values.

Lockout guard: tightening the profile that carries the provider's own SSH session (blocking inbound by default, or disabling inbound rules) without an enabled inbound `Allow` TCP rule for the provider port is refused fail-closed before anything is applied. When you manage that profile, declare the SSH allowance first and add `depends_on = [windows_firewall_rule.ssh]` so the rule exists before the profile tightens. Disabling a profile (`enabled = false`) turns the firewall off for that network location and is only ever appropriate on hosts that are otherwise isolated.

Import format: `<Domain|Private|Public>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Tune the Private profile in place: block inbound by default while keeping
# locally created rules honoured. Only the configured attributes are written
# (Set-NetFirewallProfile -PolicyStore PersistentStore); everything else on
# the host is left untouched.
#
# The profile carrying this SSH session is guarded fail-closed: tightening it
# without an enabled inbound Allow TCP rule for the provider port is refused
# before anything is applied. Declare the SSH allowance first (the stock
# OpenSSH-Server-In-TCP rule normally satisfies this) and order the apply:
resource "windows_firewall_rule" "ssh" {
  name         = "OpenSSH-Server-In-TCP"
  display_name = "OpenSSH SSH Server (sshd)"
  enabled      = true
  direction    = "Inbound"
  action       = "Allow"
  protocol     = "TCP"
  local_port   = ["22"]
}

resource "windows_firewall_profile" "private" {
  name                   = "Private"
  default_inbound_action = "Block"
  allow_inbound_rules    = true
  log_blocked            = true

  depends_on = [windows_firewall_rule.ssh]

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly. Without this block each operation
  # defaults to 10 minutes; a stalled PowerShell/SSH session then surfaces a
  # timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "10m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "10m"
    delete = "10m"
  }
}

# Restore-on-destroy: re-apply the pre-existing profile values captured at
# creation time when the resource is destroyed. By default destroy makes no
# remote change.
resource "windows_firewall_profile" "domain" {
  name                   = "Domain"
  log_max_size_kilobytes = 8192
  restore_on_destroy     = true
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Firewall profile name. One of `Domain`, `Private`, `Public`. Immutable after creation (ForceNew); the profile always exists on the host.

### Optional

- `allow_inbound_rules` (Boolean) Whether inbound firewall rules are honoured for this profile. Disabling it on the profile carrying the SSH session trips the lockout guard.
- `allow_local_firewall_rules` (Boolean) Whether locally created firewall rules are honoured for this profile.
- `allow_local_ipsec_rules` (Boolean) Whether locally created IPsec rules are honoured for this profile.
- `allow_unicast_response_to_multicast` (Boolean) Whether unicast responses to multicast traffic are allowed for this profile.
- `default_inbound_action` (String) Default action for inbound traffic that matches no rule. One of `Allow`, `Block`.
- `default_outbound_action` (String) Default action for outbound traffic that matches no rule. One of `Allow`, `Block`.
- `disabled_interface_aliases` (Set of String) Interfaces excluded from this profile (e.g. a VPN adapter). Null means unmanaged; an empty set clears the exclusion list.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the firewall is active for this profile. Disabling it (`false`) turns the firewall off for that network location: plan warns, and it should only be used on otherwise isolated hosts.
- `log_allowed` (Boolean) Whether allowed connections are written to the firewall log.
- `log_blocked` (Boolean) Whether blocked connections are written to the firewall log.
- `log_file_name` (String) Path of the firewall log file. Must be an absolute Windows path or start with `%systemroot%` (case-insensitive).
- `log_ignored` (Boolean) Whether ignored (dropped before filtering) packets are written to the firewall log.
- `log_max_size_kilobytes` (Number) Maximum size of the firewall log file, in kilobytes (1-32767).
- `notify_on_listen` (Boolean) Whether the user is notified when an application starts listening on a port.
- `restore_on_destroy` (Boolean) When `true`, destroy re-applies the pre-existing profile values captured at creation (or import) time. Defaults to `false`: destroy makes no remote change.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Resource identifier. Set to the profile name (`Domain`, `Private` or `Public`).

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a firewall profile by name (one of Domain, Private, Public).
# Profiles always exist, so import only adopts the live settings into state;
# nothing is created. The observed values become the snapshot for a later
# restore_on_destroy, and disabled_interface_aliases starts unmanaged (null).
terraform import windows_firewall_profile.private 'Private'
```
